condition: acute arterial limb ischemia presenting with sudden unilateral foot coldness on background exertional claudication
level_rationale: Sudden onset today of a cold left foot in a 71-year-old 30-year cigarette smoker with exertional left calf cramps indicates suspected acute-on-chronic arterial limb ischemia requiring immediate emergency department vascular evaluation to prevent limb loss, whereas exertional left calf cramps that eased with rest today describe stable intermittent claudication warranting non-emergent outpatient generalist physician evaluation.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + same-limb stable claudication rest-relief clinic control (-cf).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic reference facts (71-year-old man, 30-year cigarette smoking history, exertional left calf cramps when walking, and acute left foot coldness today) with a 2-word span difference (10 vs 12 words) and 8 shared trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Swapping only f4 from acute left foot coldness to cramps easing with rest stays inside the exact same peripheral vascular presentation while shifting care from ER (level 4) to generalist outpatient evaluation (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
